result.summary: The image depicts a narrow residential street with sidewalks and a faded zebra-marked crosswalk. While the low-speed nature of the street is beneficial, the lack of ADA-compliant curb ramps and worn pavement markings reduces overall pedestrian safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The existing zebra markings are heavily worn, making the crossing less visible to motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends abruptly at the curb without a sloped transition, creating a barrier for people with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Exposed Drainage Grates
hazards.description: Large metal grates located near the pedestrian path could pose a trip hazard or trap wheels.
hazards.location_in_image: Bottom left and right corners of the image.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Refresh the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install concrete curb ramps with tactile warning pads to ensure accessibility for all users.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with mixed-use buildings and continuous sidewalks in good condition. However, there is a total absence of marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or pedestrian signage, and parked cars significantly obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both sides of the street create visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross, hiding them from oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway foreground and midground

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks or signage indicating where pedestrians should cross, increasing exposure risk in a mixed-use area.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure low vehicle speeds on this narrow mixed-use street.

result.summary: The image shows a mixed-use urban intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk across a narrow one-way street. While sidewalks are present on both sides, a large vehicle parked near the corner creates a significant visual obstruction for pedestrians entering the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: A large green SUV is parked right at the corner, blocking the sightline between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra stripes of the crosswalk are somewhat worn and faded, reducing their visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove the parking space closest to the intersection on the left side to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extension (Bulb-out)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they step into the travel lane.

interventions.title: Refresh Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings.
